messages.text: Hi there — I'm Sarah, an AI researcher with HeliumDeploy. Thank you so much for taking 25 minutes to do this — it really means a lot. Honestly, the more you can share with me, the better — we're aiming for about fifteen hundred words of feedback together, so please don't worry about going long. The founders read every word of these chats, so what you say actually shapes what HD does next. As a thank-you you'll get a $75 discount code at the end. So — to kick us off, tell me about your mining setup right now. What are you running, where, and what are you trying to figure out next?
What are you trying to I have a NerdQX plus plus six point five. Terahertz, and I'm running a bid axe on my own node in my own pool. Through five stratum. Operating system.

Nice — so you've got the NerdQaxe++ at 6.5 TH and a Bitaxe pointed at your own node through Public Pool on stratum. That's a real setup. Running your own pool against your own node — why'd you go that route instead of just pointing at Solo CK or one of the public solo pools?
Because the latency was so bad, it was, like, a hundred ms.
Hundred ms is rough — yeah, that'll eat into your effective hashrate. So you stood up your own node and pool to cut that down. How low did you get the latency once it was all local?
Two, to four m s. It's nice.

Two to four ms — that's a massive jump. Okay, so you're clearly deep in the technical side. Walk me through how you got here — did you start with the Bitaxe first and then add the NerdQaxe, or the other way around?

Started with the BitX first, then I went with the NerdX. Then I just decided to make my own version pool. I got a pie five. And did it all through chat GPT. He set it up for me. And I got my own nodes on, uh, my PC. And I got a couple on the pie five.

That's awesome — Pi 5 running Public Pool, ChatGPT walking you through setup, multiple nodes across your PC and the Pi. You're basically running your own mini-infrastructure. 

So when you hit a wall during setup — like something ChatGPT couldn't solve — where do you go? Discord, Reddit, YouTube, somewhere else?
Uh, yeah. I went to Google sometimes. I went back and forth between, uh, the Google AI and chat GPT. Between the two of them, um, I got it worked out.
Got it — bouncing between Gemini and ChatGPT until one of them cracks it. Smart. So no Discord, no Reddit threads — just the AIs and Google?

Yeah. I didn't use Discord for anything. I have a Discord account, but um, the only thing I use Discord account for was I was having trouble with axe. Uh, one of the apps in there. The X. app, uh, when they updated it, it wouldn't load. It wouldn't load right. So I used chat GPT and actually had to rebuild the whole app It was the the the version that the devs put out was only six k, and it needed to be, um, or mine was fourteen k, and it needed to be six k or something. I had to rebuild the whole app.
Wait — so you rebuilt AxeOS yourself because the dev release was broken for your unit? That's serious tinkering. Walk me through that — you forked it, recompiled, flashed it back on?

Yep. Recompiled it. Took about three and a half hours Just sat there for three and a half hours rebuilding. Um, Yeah. Kip, uh, Chad GPT found that it wasn't compatible with pie five. The version that they put out was compatible with older pies. But PIE five was looking for um, sixteen k pages, and we had to rebuild the apps for four for four k pages.

That's wild — three and a half hours recompiling AxeOS for 4k pages on the Pi 5 because the official build assumed older Pi page sizes. So you're doing kernel-level stuff that 99% of Bitaxe owners will never touch.

Let me ask — when you're that deep in it, what else are you tinkering with on the hardware side? Overclocking, custom cooling, anything like that?

Thank Yeah. Overclocking. I got my nerd access six point five terahertz. I got an Noctua fan on the back of it. And I got a PSU, uh, uh, hundred and eighty watt PSU I had to upgrade. And I got a fifteen a amp in the NERDACS. I had to upgrade that from the the stock one. To support all the power extra power.
Beautiful — Noctua on the back, 180W PSU upgrade, 15A line into the NerdQaxe. So you pushed it past stock. What's it hashing at now with the OC, and what's your J/TH looking like?

This has happened a six point five. Pretty steady. It drops down a little bit, though. I'm I. logging it right now, and I'm gonna send it a chat GPT. I have a suspicion that I might have a little bit of a laggy one chip on this thing, but for for the most part, it's pretty good, but I'm suspecting it may be a little bit, uh, one like I said, the one chip might be doing something because I've had this NerdX for a while, and its highest hit is only four g. My bid access hit eighty g. My bid access at eight g, four g. This thing here, it struggles to hit five hundred million. Uh, the nerd x, I'm kinda wondering why.

Interesting — so the Bitaxe at 1.5 TH has hit 8 gigahash on a share, and the NerdQaxe at 6.5 TH is struggling to hit 500 mega. That's backwards from what variance should look like. You're right to suspect a chip.

Are you planning to RMA it, or are you gonna try diagnosing it yourself first? Like swap chips, reflow, something like that?

No. I don't know yet. I'm doing I'm I. logging it right now. Because every time I do a log, Chad GPT tells me that one chip is like, two percent behind, but it's not a big deal. Um, most of them do that. So it's not a it's not a huge lag. It's just, like, a little bit. But it's there. So I think that's why I can't ever get big hits. The bid axe at one point five terahertz, had a I had a a d g hit the other day, and then, like, the next day, I had a eight g hit on the bit ax. But for some reason, the nerd ax it just can't get there. I got one four gig I got one four g hit, and then about took a couple months got a two g hit. But other than that, I've gotten like a a a one g hit one time and then a one g hit the other time. And that's it. It hardly even gets over five hundred million now. But from my logs and from everything, everything looks great. Everything looks stable. My temperatures are down. My fans are only at fifty five percent. I can the the temp temperatures are at, like, fifty degree fifty five degrees. For the chip and, like, fifty six degrees for the VR. Like, I can't even get them to sixty degrees. The cooling is really good. Can't understand it.

Yeah that's a real puzzle — temps are gorgeous, OC is stable, but the big-difficulty shares just aren't landing. Statistically a 6.5 TH unit should be hitting multi-gig shares way more often than a 1.5 TH Bitaxe. Something's off.

Let me pull
That's what I'm saying. And me about it. I mean, it's crazy.

Right? It's mathematically weird. The Bitaxe is outperforming a unit 4x its size on big shares — that's not variance, that's a signal.

Let me pull up the NerdQaxe page real quick. So you're on a 6.0 originally I assume, and you OC'd to 6.5.
No. No. No. No. It's a it's a four point eight. I got it overclocked to six point five. It's a NerdQX plus plus. Four point eight one, just like the first one. You know? Just a four point eight.

Got it — four point eight stock, pushed to six point five. So you're already 35% over stock. That's aggressive but with your cooling setup it makes sense.

Question — when you bought the NerdQaxe, did you compare it against anything else, or did you go straight for it?

Uh, no. I already had the BIDEX. So if anything, I guess I'm comparing it to my BIDEX. Which is just a monster. Like I said, that BIDEX is just forming it in every way. ADG hit, eight eight g hit, You know, it's I don't know. It's weird. Uh, I just got another two point five g hit the other day with the bit ax. It's just crazy.

Yeah the Bitaxe is being a beast. Honestly if I were you I'd be eyeing the RMA path on the NerdQaxe — that chip lag is real signal.

What's the RMA pass? I heard you say that before. What's that?

Oh sorry — RMA is "Return Merchandise Authorization." Basically: you contact HD support, explain the chip is underperforming, they walk you through diagnostics, and if it's defective they swap it or refund. Given you have logs showing that one chip running 2% behind plus the wildly low big-share hits, you'd have a solid case.

HD has a return policy on the product page — free return shipping in the US, I think 30 days. Have you owned the NerdQaxe long enough that you'd be past the

If I had if I had one shift that that one shift say like, when I asked Chad GPT, he told me it's not a big deal. It's only, like, one to two percent behind the other chips. It was a little bit more, then it would be a big deal. But he say they all do that. Is that true?

Honestly? Kinda yes and kinda no. ChatGPT is right that no two chips on a multi-chip board hash identically — there's always some variance, and 1-2% is within normal binning tolerance. That part is true.

But here's the thing — chip variance of 1-2% would NOT explain your big-share problem. Big shares are about luck on the nonce space, and a healthy 6.5 TH unit should statistically be landing multi-gig shares way more often than a 1.5 TH Bitaxe. The fact that your Bitaxe is hitting 8G and the NerdQaxe is stuck under 500M for months — that's not chip variance. That's something else.

Could be the chip is producing valid shares but the high-difficulty ones are getting rejected, could be a pool/stratum config issue specific to that unit, could be the chip is silently dropping nonces in a certain range. Have you compared the accepted

Everything is good, though. I'm getting zero percent errors. I get no rejects. I'll have, like, twenty thousand I'll have, like, twenty thousand shares accepted in, like, five rejects. You know? It's can't there's no hardware errors in my logs. It's just weird. Everything looks perfect on it. It just doesn't get good hits. Maybe I'm just overthinking it. Because the bid ax is so has been hit just getting lucky. You know? I think maybe I'm just overlooking it. It's probably just bad luck.

Yeah honestly — you might be right. With 20,000 accepted and 5 rejected, error rate is basically zero, temps are great, OC is stable. The unit is healthy. It really might just be variance. Solo mining at these hashrates is brutal on the nerves because the law of large numbers needs WAY more time than feels intuitive. The Bitaxe is getting lucky, the NerdQaxe is getting unlucky, and over a long enough horizon they'll both regress toward the mean.

Okay let me shift gears for a sec. You're clearly deep in this — Pi 5 pool, recompiled AxeOS, Noctua mod, PSU upgrade, OC to 6.5. Where does this go next? Like what's the next mod or next miner on your list?
Probably, uh, what's that one that's twelve terahertz? The octate octax or something, or I'll just get another NerdQX plus plus since this one sucks ass.

Ha — yeah the NerdOctaxe is the 12 TH one, that's HD's next step up. Let me pull it up actually — wait, let me show you the comparison view first since you're weighing options. There — that comparison table on the homepage. NerdOctaxe is $469 for 12 TH, the Nexus S1 is $650. Did you ever scroll down to this one when you were on the site, or is this the first time seeing it?
Yeah. I've seen it. Probably just gonna get through. Nerd q x ref six point one for two forty nine.
Got it — so you'd just double up on the same model rather than step up to the Octaxe or Nexus. Why?

Yeah. I don't know. The O. is just a little bit too much. I want the this five hundred is just is is what's doing it. If it was a little bit cheaper, I'd probably go with that one. But I just can't I don't know. Six terahertz for the two fifty is just really worth it to me. This nerd nerd octane is just a little too much. If it was, like, three fifty, or, like, three eight I don't know. Under four hundred dollars maybe, I'd get it. It's just too much money. It's just a little too much.

Yeah — so $469 crosses a mental line for you, but $249 doesn't. And it's not the $/TH math, because the Octaxe is actually slightly better $/TH than the NerdQaxe.

Why is the threshold there? Like why is $400 the wall?

I just don't wanna spend that much more, uh, on this hobby, I guess. I don't know. It's not it's not four hundred. It says four ninety nine right there. Five hundred. It's just too much I just don't wanna spend five hundred on another machine. But I I would spend half that too. I would spend two fifty on the nerd.
Got it —
On the, uh, yeah, that one.

Yeah — so $250 is your hobby ceiling per unit. Anything above that and you're like "nah, not for fun money." Makes sense.

So you'd rather have two 6.5 TH units running than one 12 TH unit, even though they cost about the same in total. Why two over one? Is it the redundancy, the variance from two independent units, just twice the fun to tinker with?

No. It's just that you get one separately. Don't wanna spot it in. I didn't spend all the money at one time. You might spend two hundred and fifty dollars and then you might to get one, and then maybe six to eight months later, you know, you might spend another two hundred and fifty dollars to just get one more when you got some extra money hanging around. But it's not I'm not to the point where it's I'm spending five hundred dollars at a time. You know? Maybe just two hundred and fifty every couple months. That's okay. That's why I got two.

Got it — so it's pure cash flow. You drip $250 every few months when you've got spare money. $500 at once feels like a real bite. The "buy more later" pattern keeps it feeling like hobby spending instead of investment spending.

That's super clear. Okay — switching gears. Where does the NerdQaxe physically live in your house? Like what room is it in?
It's in my spare room. Um, I got my com it's like a computer room. Office type of room.
Computer room — makes sense. Is that because that's where the desk/network gear already is, or because you don't want it elsewhere — noise, heat, family,
Actually, my note is That's where my node is and everything, so I'm just trying to keep it close to the node. And, um, my router. Gotta have that low latency. Now I'm saying?

Right — keep everything tight to the node and router for that 2-4ms latency. Smart.

Oh, no. No, Sarah. We are wired in. No no Wi Fi here. We are all wired in Ethernet.

I don't I don't see that necessary to do minor uh, to plug my minor in hardwire that in. Probably not necessary. You know? Probably not gonna make that much difference on my public. On my solo odds. You know?

Wait — so the miners themselves are on WiFi, just the node and Pi are wired? I had you mixed up. Got it. And at 30ms WiFi to your local pool, you're not bottlenecked by that — the Bitaxe and NerdQaxe don't need lower than that to solo effectively. Makes sense to pass on the Ethernet module.

Okay let me ask about something else. You're in (address hidden), Georgia — and summer's basically here. Does the heat ever change how you run these? Like underclock, move them, anything seasonal?
No. Not really. I keep my house pretty cold. I got my AC on about seventy right now, so she stays pretty pretty crispy in here.

Crispy — love it. Yeah at 70 inside, the miners don't really stress the AC and you don't need to do anything seasonal. Good deal.

Nah. Not really. I mean, I might see some things on Facebook from these little Facebook groups that I'm a part of, but I don't really do much of the disc Discord and all that other stuff that you're saying.

I don't know what they're called. I can't remember. Some crypto bit x thing. I can't remember.

Let me show you one more thing — HD's thinking about adding something like this to the customer dashboard — opt-in leaderboard ranking top miners by hashrate, you'd see where you sit. Would you actually use that, or is that not your thing?

I mean, yeah, I would use it, but, uh, probably I mean, I would use it. It's pretty cool, but I wouldn't be at the top. I'm not I'm not into it that much. I just got a, you know, two two little machines here, so I probably wouldn't ever look at it because I know I wouldn't be at the top.

Yeah — fair. If you know you're not in the top tier, the leaderboard becomes background noise. It's really only motivating if you think you could climb it.
